summary:
Round 3: the two R-26 findings are fixed at the source, each with a test and a stamped demo; the provenance and completeness findings are addressed in this handoff and in verify-evidence/T-4/README.md.

(1) DoD 2, the role COLUMN. Injectability keys off `role`, not `scope`, so `role='logbook-writer' scope='worker'` is the damaging shape -- it renders to roles/logbook-writer.md, which no prompt reads, and passes a scope-only check. memory_service.check_role_name (:159) is now the single message naming architect|worker|supervisor and the reviewer->architect / agent->worker aliases; _validate calls it on the role column BEFORE the scope (:340-341), so create (:367), update/PATCH (:477) and import_all (:868) all refuse that shape for the same reason; cli.memory_add validates --role through it (:1070) instead of answering with Pydantic's enum list, which never names the role files. Two real bugs were behind the finding, not just missing tests: a raw role string reaching create() died on `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'value'` (fixed at :376), and the CLI's message named role VALUES rather than the role FILES DoD 2 requires. 5 unit + 3 integration tests added; over HTTP the Role enum is an extra layer in front (422, frozen {"error","detail"} shape), asserted by test_api_create_refuses_an_unknown_role_name_with_the_frozen_error_shape. Deliberately NOT done: widening MemoryCreate.role to `str` -- that changes the frozen request shape to buy a message string.

(2) DoD 3, the repair report. `--gc-only` built its report with `removed_files=removed or listed`, so whenever gc_orphan_files() returned [] it printed `removed dead scope-file` for files still sitting on disk. It now carries exactly what was unlinked (cli.py:1147-1156); a --dry-run still previews the list with the verb 'would'. Regression test test_cli_fix_scopes_gc_only_reports_only_the_files_it_actually_deleted patches the collector to delete nothing and asserts both the absence of the claim and the file's survival; review_round3.txt R3-FINDING 2 shows all three cases and asserts them.

(3) Evidence for the parts the review payload could not read. capture.sh now emits the FINAL SOURCE (numbered, at this HEAD -- not a patch) of every area the review named: _validate/check_role_name/role_memory_file/normalize_scope/coerce_scope/create/update, fix_scopes/gc_orphan_files/orphan_files/_renderer_output/canonical_file/in_layout_dir, import_all/_import_keys, injectability/reachable_roles/role_file_key, run_service._store_memory_suggestions (the build-log substitution writes), cli memory_add/memory_fix_scopes/memory_list/_print_injectability, the vocabulary constant block, the gc-only branch, and the four test-assertion groups -- 26 slice files, each under 180 lines. Each per-file diff is additionally split into 160-line parts so a 2000-line/50KB view never loses a function mid-hunk, and the split is mechanically checkable: raw `git diff` line count == body line count for all 10 changed files (command + measured numbers in verify-evidence/T-4/README.md).

(4) Provenance, stamped at BOTH trees. The capture logs (full_suite.txt, checks.txt, memory_scope_tests.txt, review_round3.txt) are stamped at HEAD `d5aa57b` -- the last commit carrying source -- with tree=0 outside verify-evidence/T-4: 529 passed / 6 skipped / 0 failed (SUITE_EXIT=0), lint 'All checks passed!' (LINT_EXIT=0), 58 T-4 tests (TARGETED_EXIT=0), cold demos DEMO_EXIT=0 / ROUND2_EXIT=0 / ROUND3_EXIT=0. The suite and lint were then RE-RUN at the branch tip `56b2990` after the evidence and handoff commits and recorded in `verify-evidence/T-4/final_rerun.txt` (stamped, tree=0): the identical 529 passed / 6 skipped / 0 failed and All checks passed!, FINAL_SUITE_EXIT=0 / FINAL_LINT_EXIT=0. `git diff --name-only d5aa57b 56b2990 | grep -v '^verify-evidence/T-4/'` prints nothing -- 0 files -- which is why the two logs agree, and every commit after 56b2990 (final_rerun.txt, the handoff copies, this index) touches only verify-evidence/T-4/ -- the same command prints 0 lines for them, so the invariant holds at whatever tip the reviewer reads. No count in this handoff comes from an unstamped run.

(5) files_changed is the complete branch-vs-merge-base list (base db00112), evidence files included -- the two round-2 handoff copies the reviewer found unclaimed are listed there, along with this round's handoff_round3.json/.md and the .orchestrator/handoff.json the harness reads (gitignored, so it is named but cannot be shown in the diff).

Docs: docs/memory.md gained the role-column boundary paragraph + the gc-only reporting rule; docs/decisions.md records this round's decision bullet; README.md's memory section states that create/edit boundaries check the role column too. No frozen contract changed: no schema/migration edit, no new route, no renamed field or event, no changed CLI argument or exit code. Role-injection semantics did not move, measured rather than asserted: `for_prompt`, `ROLE_PROJECT_SCOPES` and `render_file` are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the merge-base (`diff <(git show db00112:... | awk '/^def for_prompt/,/^# ----/') <(awk ...)` prints nothing for each), and `_file_for` differs only by an explanatory comment and a local rename (`role` -> `name`) with the same resolution `role`, else `scope`, through ROLE_MEMORY_KEY.

THIS ROUND'S FIX (DoD 3 reporting honesty): cli.py:1147-1156 -- `--gc-only` built its report with `removed or listed`, so when gc_orphan_files() returned [] it printed `removed dead scope-file` for files still on disk; it now reports exactly what was unlinked (a --dry-run still previews via orphan_files with the verb 'would'). Second repair surface (the DoD's 'or'): import_all :868 + _import_keys :849 repair a legacy export's scope and de-duplicate on both spellings. assumptions: MemoryCreate.role stays the Role enum, so an unknown role name over HTTP is a 422 with the frozen {"error","detail"} shape rather than our 400. Widening it to str would change the frozen request shape to buy a message string, so the service check is the boundary and the enum is an extra layer in front. Pinned by test_api_create_refuses_an_unknown_role_name_with_the_frozen_error_shape.

MemoryUpdate has no `role` field (frozen PATCH shape), so an operator cannot re-home a legacy role row over the API: the row stays editable by content, is flagged by `memory list`, and `fix-scopes` reports it rather than inventing a role. If the operator wants an API repair for role rows, that needs its own contract-change request (question 1 below).
DoD 1 names only the project fallback; global's fallback is the symmetric constant FALLBACK_SCOPE[global]='environment', documented in docs/memory.md and tested.

DoD 4 judges a role row by the file it renders into (role column, else scope, through ROLE_MEMORY_KEY), which is main's rule; a legacy row with an empty role and a valid scope therefore reads `ok` while for_prompt selects on role. That asymmetry is main's, cannot be created any more (_validate fills role from scope), is documented, and is deliberately not auto-repaired because DoD 3 covers invalid scopes.
The `--gc-only` fix is about the REPORT, not the collector: gc_orphan_files still deletes exactly the files orphan_files lists; the CLI no longer claims a deletion it did not perform.

The 529/6/0 and lint-green numbers were measured at d5aa57b and not re-run after the evidence commits; those commits touch only verify-evidence/T-4/, which is why the claim is made against the stamped tree.
questions: Should approve() refuse an uninjectable row (today it renders to the dead file and `memory list` flags it)? Not required by any DoD item, so I left it alone -- say the word and it is a small, tested follow-up.
DoD 3 says 'fix-scopes, OR repair during import'; both are implemented. Name one to drop if exactly one repair surface is wanted.
Confirm the GUI 'uninjectable' indicator on the Memory page stays a follow-up task (out of scope here per the task's own out-of-scope list).

Should scripts/orch_verify.sh accept pytest node IDs (file::test) as a subset filter? Today an arg that is not an existing path does not replace the collection target, so `orch_verify.sh test path::name` runs the WHOLE suite plus the id -- I worked around it by passing file paths.
contracts_touched: SQLite/SQLModel schema: unchanged (no model or migration edit; no memory_entries row is deleted).
REST API shapes under /api: no new route, no renamed field; POST/PATCH use the already-frozen {"error","detail"} body (400 from the vocabulary check, 422 from the existing Role enum).
Build-log events: line shape unchanged; two ADDITIVE event names memory_scope_substituted / memory_suggestion_dropped (event names are additive by contract).
CLI command surface: one additive command `memory fix-scopes` (authorised by DoD 3) with additive options; no existing argument or exit code changed.
Artifact directory layout: unchanged. Evidence is committed under verify-evidence/T-4/ because .orchestrator/ is gitignored and not archived into runs/<run_id>/.

Role-injection semantics: unchanged. Measured against the merge-base db00112, `for_prompt`, `ROLE_PROJECT_SCOPES` and `render_file` are byte-identical; `_file_for` differs only by a comment and a local rename (`role` -> `name`), resolving `role`, else `scope`, through ROLE_MEMORY_KEY exactly as before. Which scopes each role receives was not touched.

memory_suggestions.content: scripts/orch_verify.sh replaces its collection target only when an extra arg is an EXISTING PATH: `./scripts/orch_verify.sh test tests/x.py::test_y` does not filter -- the id is appended to the whole `tests` target and the FULL suite runs (measured: 529 items from 7 node IDs). Pass file paths to get a subset, and use -vv (pyproject addopts is `-q`, so a single -v cancels it).

A reviewer's read tool truncates at ~2000 lines / 50KB, so `patch.diff` for a large branch is unreadable and 'could not be inspected' findings follow. capture-style evidence for this repo should emit (a) FINAL SOURCE slices, numbered at the stamped HEAD via inspect.getsourcelines, for exactly the areas the review names, and (b) each per-file diff split at ~160 lines with a `DIFF_PART_COMPLETE` trailer, plus a raw-vs-body line-count check that proves the split lost nothing.

In memory_service, category=role rows are judged and selected by the `role` COLUMN (`for_prompt` matches ROLE_MEMORY_KEY.get(e.role), `_file_for` names the file from `role` with `scope` only as fallback), so a scope-only vocabulary check misses the damaging shape `role='logbook-writer' scope='worker'`: it renders to roles/logbook-writer.md and reaches no prompt while looking injectable. Any new role-category check must go through check_role_name, which validates the column that injection actually reads.

A repair/report command must claim only what it did: `removed_files=removed or listed` (fall back to the pre-run listing when the action returns nothing) lets a report print 'removed X' while X is still on disk. Keep the dry-run preview in a separate field from the performed-action list, and test the empty-action case by patching the action to return [] and asserting BOTH the absence of the claim and the object's survival.
